title: Feature Context
description:
What a feature is SUPPOSED to do, assembled by the research fleet from human-authored sources. Written by research, read by the QA fleet, and used as the oracle for every finding.

The governing rule: research agents QUOTE AND LINK. They never paraphrase a source into a new requirement, and they never author one. If an agent could write a requirement here, the QA fleet would be graded against a truth the system invented for itself, and the whole falsifiability claim collapses. Anything without a human-authored source belongs in `unknowns`, not in `requirements`.

summary.description: One paragraph, assembled only from quoted sources. Not an agent's own description.

trackerKeys.description: Jira/Linear keys this feature spans, e.g. ['EXM-412'].

staleAfter.description: Context rots as tickets change. Past this, the fleet warns rather than silently testing against an old spec.

sources.description: Every human-authored artifact consulted. A requirement may only cite a source listed here.

id.description: Local id referenced by requirements, e.g. 's1'.

author.description: Who wrote it. Anonymous sources are weaker evidence.

requirements.description: Testable statements of intended behaviour. Each one becomes a candidate oracle.

statement.description: The requirement as a testable assertion. Must be supported verbatim by `quote`.

quote.description: The human-authored text this rests on, copied exactly. Empty means the requirement was inferred, which is not allowed: move it to `unknowns`.

sourceIds.description: At least one. A requirement with no source is invalid by construction.

confidence.description: explicit: the source states it outright. implied: the source clearly entails it. contested: sources disagree - see `conflictsWith`.

conflictsWith.description: Other requirement ids this contradicts. Conflicts are surfaced to the human, never resolved by an agent.

axisHints.description: Which test axes this requirement is relevant to.

unknowns.description: Behaviour nobody wrote down. This list is a deliverable, not a failure: it tells the human exactly where the fleet is testing blind, and it is where an agent's guesses are quarantined so they can never become oracles.

why.description: What the fleet cannot judge without an answer.

guess.description: The agent's best inference. Explicitly NOT usable as an oracle - it lives here precisely so it cannot be cited as one.

knownIssues.description: Already-reported or accepted behaviour. Suppresses re-reporting, which is the fastest way to make a team stop reading the output.

regressionHistory.description: Bugs this feature has had before. The single best predictor of where it will break again, and the main input to test prioritisation.

provenance.description: How this context was assembled, so a stale or thin oracle is visible rather than assumed.

connectors.description: Which integrations actually answered. A connector that failed means a whole class of source is missing.

coverage.description: Honesty about the oracle itself: a context built from two comments is not the same as one built from a written spec.
